newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares slip despite selective demand.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares slip despite selective demand.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell slightly on Tuesday despite heavy demand for a variety of stocks, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) report said.
The CMA overall index slipped 0.66 points to 357.83 in above average volume of 74.42 million pounds ($22 million).
Pyramids Breweries was the most active share in Tuesday's market, rising 5.25 pounds to 110.25 after trading in 21.55 million pounds.

Mohammed Abdullah, managing director of Intercapital brokerage, said increase in the stock was probably generated by a strong performance in the brewing company's London-listed Global Depositary Receipt (GDR).

"There isn't a lot of liquidity available for the breweries in Egypt. This good performance was directly affected by the GDR. It is one of the illiquid stocks in Cairo. Some brokerages don't deal in it and it is not very popular," he said.
He was referring to the Islamic ban on alcohol, which some brokers said was behind last year's initial broker reluctance to make the most of a public share offer in the stock.

Abdullah said market rumours that Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries would distribute a dividend of 13 pounds -- two pounds higher than last year's -- pushed that stock to second place in the day's list of 10 most active shares.
Eipico closed one pound higher at 208 after trade in shares worth 6.18 million pounds.

Eastern Company did well, with investors making the most of a recent downward trend to buy up shares in the tobacco company, Abdullah said. The stock rose 0.94 pounds to 85.99 after trading in six million pounds.
Institutional buying helped Commercial International Bank (CIB) close 0.25 pounds higher at 72.8 after trade in five million pounds, Abdullah said.
"Large institutions saw CIB's low dividend as a positive sign that the bank wants to strengthen its balance sheet. This interest has put the price back to what it was," he said.

CIB said last month it would pay a two pound dividend per share for 1996. It gave shareholders a 20 pound dividend in 1995 and in August 1996 it split its shares 10-for-one. investor disappointment at the dividend pushed CIB's price down recently.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 498.19 points from 502.62 points on Monday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 262.45 from 261.99 points.
Out of the 92 shares traded, 33 rose, 32 fell and the other 27 ended the day unchanged.
